skill.name: auth
skill.description: Authentication and access control skill for Next.js 15 + Supabase applications. Use when implementing user authentication, protecting routes, managing user sessions, enforcing role-based access control (admin/member), or working with multi-tenant family-based data isolation. Covers login/logout, registration with email verification, OAuth (GitHub), route protection for Server Components and Server Actions, admin-only features, and multi-tenant data access patterns.
skill.summary: Implement server-side Supabase authentication, role checks, route protection, and family-based tenant isolation in Next.js 15.
skill.author: BOM-98

security_audit.summary: All 62 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, documentation examples, placeholder URLs, and auth schema descriptions. No command execution, reconnaissance, environment-file reading, or live network request exists in the reviewed skill files. One high-severity semantic issue remains: the registration design stores SSNs and other sensitive personal data in Supabase user metadata.

remediation.issue: Sensitive personal data is placed in Supabase user metadata.
remediation.suggestion: Remove SSNs and similar data from auth metadata. Store necessary fields in encrypted, access-controlled tables with retention and access logging safeguards.

content.value_statement: Authentication mistakes can expose accounts and tenant data. This skill provides Next.js 15 and Supabase patterns for sessions, route protection, roles, and family isolation.
actual_capabilities: Protect Next.js Server Components, pages, and layouts with reusable server authentication helpers.
Enforce authentication in Server Actions through requireAuth and authorization errors.
Restrict admin pages and actions, and conditionally render admin controls.
Isolate household data through family membership checks and row-level security guidance.
Implement email login, logout, registration, email verification, and GitHub OAuth.
Configure Supabase SSR cookies, middleware refresh, and server-side token validation.
limitations: The guidance assumes FinTracker helper paths, route groups, and database tables.
The skill provides documentation and examples, not executable source files or database migrations.
The registration model places SSNs and other personal data in user metadata, which requires redesign before production use.
The skill does not provide complete tests, rate limiting, audit logging, or production secrets management.

output_examples.input: Protect the dashboard and every child route.
output: Place the server authentication redirect in the dashboard layout.
Keep authorization checks inside every data-changing Server Action.
Validate the current user with the Supabase server before rendering protected content.

output_examples.input: Review a family settings update for tenant isolation.
output: Authenticate the caller before reading profile data.
Compare the requested family identifier with the caller's server-derived family identifier.
Reject mismatches before any database write and retain row-level security as defense in depth.

output_examples.input: Assess the registration flow before production release.
output_examples.output: The flow needs sensitive-data redesign. Remove SSNs and similar personal data from auth metadata, minimize collection, and use protected storage.

best_practices: Validate users server-side with Supabase getUser before making authorization decisions.
Enforce authentication, role, and tenant checks at every data-changing server boundary.
Keep credentials outside version control and store sensitive identity data in protected application tables.
anti_patterns: Do not rely only on middleware to protect Server Actions or other POST requests.
Do not trust client-side role state or tenant identifiers for authorization.
Do not store SSNs or similar personal data in client-readable authentication metadata.

faq.question: Which frameworks does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It targets Next.js 15 App Router applications using Supabase SSR authentication.

faq.question: Does the skill install authentication code?
faq.answer: No. It provides project-specific workflows, architecture references, and TypeScript examples.

faq.question: Which sign-in methods are documented?
faq.answer: It covers email and password authentication, email verification, logout, and GitHub OAuth.

faq.question: How are routes and Server Actions protected?
faq.answer: Pages use server-side redirect helpers. Server Actions use explicit authentication and authorization helpers before protected work.

faq.question: How does tenant isolation work?
faq.answer: Each user belongs to a family. Server checks compare family membership, while row-level security provides another enforcement layer.

faq.question: Is the registration model ready for production?
faq.answer: No. Remove SSNs and other sensitive personal data from auth metadata before production use.
